title: Consider covered calls on major indices
summary: Covered calls on major indices such as the S&P 500 and Nasdaq can pay more per unit of risk than covered calls on single stocks, especially when the VIX is in the mid-20s. The index also removes idiosyncratic single-stock risk.

steps.caption: An index like the S&P 500: no single company can gap it on its own news.
Realized volatility of the index is lower than for most single stocks.
With the VIX in the mid-20s, index implied volatility is elevated.
The gap is large: you get paid more per unit of risk than on many single names.

takeaways: Index covered calls can pay more per unit of risk than single-stock covered calls.
A VIX in the mid-20s makes index premium richer.
An index removes idiosyncratic single-stock risk.
caveats: A short clip with no numbers beyond the VIX level; the chart uses illustrative values.
